name: AI-generated ad creative retainer
one_liner: Produce monthly batches of AI-generated video ads (AI avatars/UGC-style) for brands already spending heavily on Meta ads.
customer: DTC/e-commerce brands and apps with large paid-social budgets
offer: 20 AI-generated short-form video ads per month
how_it_makes_money: Monthly retainer, stated example: $2,000/month for 20 ads; the guest says 10 such clients gets you to $20K/month
startup_cost: low (AI video tool subscriptions; no amount stated)
evidence: 'I will create 20 ads a month for you for $2,000. These people will have the budget because they already spend 500k per month on meta ads' (FNMNQrCbHnk)
An app 'scaled from 0 to 20 million in annual recurring revenue just with AI ads' (FNMNQrCbHnk)
risks: Crowded market of AI UGC agencies
Ad performance is what clients judge, and you can't control it
Platform rules on disclosing AI content and synthetic people
Tool costs and capabilities change fast

name: Vertical white-label CRM (GoHighLevel SaaS)
one_liner: Rebrand GoHighLevel as a CRM/marketing system for one profession and sell it as a monthly subscription.
customer: Small professional firms in one niche (insurance agents, gyms, clinics, dentists, vets, lawyers, estate agents)
offer: Niche-branded CRM, automations and lead follow-up built on white-labelled HighLevel
how_it_makes_money: Monthly SaaS subscription, $97 to $2,000/month per account; HighLevel itself costs about $300/month
time_to_first_revenue: unknown (one company reportedly went from 0 to $1.8M in 11 months)
evidence: '67 businesses making between 50,000 and 500,000 per month... all white labeling the same $300 software' (HWPQPTOG6Ew)
Agent CRM for insurance agents: $97/month, over 1,000 customers (HWPQPTOG6Ew)
7 Figure Docs: ~$1,500/month across 3,000 medical clinics; the price came from an AI search, so treat it as weak (HWPQPTOG6Ew)
PushPress Grow (gym software) is 'literally just highlevel white labelled' (HWPQPTOG6Ew)
risks: The video itself says marketing is the hard part
Depends on HighLevel's platform and pricing
Churn among small businesses
Onboarding and support work grows with each customer
UK/EU GDPR obligations for the client data you hold

name: Automated competitor-intelligence email
one_liner: A fully automated weekly email reporting what a client's top competitors did.
customer: SMBs and marketing teams that track competitors
offer: Every Friday, an email summarising the client's top 3 competitors
evidence: 'Pay me $300 a month. I'll send you an email every Friday with your top three competitors, fully automated' (H34wM31A6_4)
risks: Only a pitch example in the video, no paying customers shown
Easy to copy
Hard to prove value, so churn risk
Scraping legality and reliability

name: AI automation implementation agency (Gumloop)
one_liner: Build and maintain AI workflows on Gumloop for companies that lack in-house builders.
customer: SMBs and enterprise teams adopting AI automation
offer: Workflow build-outs plus ongoing maintenance and retainers
how_it_makes_money: Project fees and monthly retainers (no prices stated)
evidence: Gumloop hired one of its community experts to build workflows for its largest enterprise accounts: 'now he has a new career' (H34wM31A6_4)
Framed as getting in early, like starting an agency on Zapier in its first years (H34wM31A6_4)
risks: No pricing or revenue evidence
Tied to one young YC-backed vendor
Selling usually needs discovery calls
Commoditisation

name: Bulk AI product descriptions for e-commerce
one_liner: Generate product descriptions in bulk for online stores using cheap LLM models.
offer: Thousands of SEO product descriptions per batch
how_it_makes_money: Per-batch fee: 'thousands of product descriptions for a couple hundred bucks'
evidence: Weak, listicle mention only: 'generate thousands of product descriptions for a couple hundred bucks... sell those... to e-commerce brands' (E8ARq-4ous8)
risks: Low price and heavily commoditised
Clients can do it themselves with ChatGPT
Probably better as an upsell; a multilingual EN/PT/ES version could stand out

name: Niche hobby companion app (board-game CRM)
one_liner: A vibe-coded subscription app for one passionate hobby community, e.g. tracking board-game collections, plays and game nights.
offer: Personal CRM app: collection tracking, game-night scheduling with friends, stats
evidence: Weak, idea only: 'vibe code an app for board game lovers... charge 10 bucks a month and you don't need that many people to hit 10k a year' (GER_aZkQQ_0)
The speaker has a live app-store app despite not knowing how to code (GER_aZkQQ_0)
risks: No demand validation
Getting users is the hard part
Free incumbents such as BoardGameGeek
Low ceiling

name: AI influencer accounts with brand sponsorships
one_liner: Create and grow AI-generated influencer personas on Instagram/TikTok and sell sponsored posts.
offer: Sponsored stories and reels from an AI persona
how_it_makes_money: Sponsorship fees; claims that brands pay 'hundreds of thousands' per story or reel, and one persona earns $10M/year
evidence: 'She's making $10 million per year in revenue and she doesn't exist' (FNMNQrCbHnk); the claim is unverified
risks: Audience growth is slow and luck-driven
Platform policies and disclosure rules on AI content
Outlier claims
Reputational and ethical concerns
